Fluid catalytic cracking upgrades heavy hydrocarbons without added hydrogen. Typical feeds are heavy vacuum gas oil and, in some configurations, atmospheric residue; the process produces gasoline and olefin-rich C3/C4 streams suitable for alkylation.
The FCC unit comprises reactor-regenerator, fractionation and wet-gas/gas-plant sections. Coke deposited on the circulating zeolitic catalyst is burned during continuous catalyst regeneration.

Gas separation recovers C1 to C5-plus fractions from refinery off-gases by compression, absorption and distillation; products may include fuel gas, propane/butane LPG, C4 fractions and light gasoline.
Visbreaking is a non-catalytic thermal process applied to atmospheric or vacuum residues to reduce residue viscosity and form gas, naphtha, distillate and a visbroken residue.
